newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan finance minister angrily denies impropriety.
newsitem.headline: Japan finance minister angrily denies impropriety.

text.p: Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka angrily denied reports on Wednesday that he had received improper political contributions and threatened to sue the newspapers involved.

The reports in two Japanese papers, the Mainichi Shimbun and a tabloid, said that a witness in an open court hearing last month had testified that Mitsuzuka had received money from a stock speculator convicted in a share manipulation scheme.
"The report is completely groundless," Mitsuzuka told reporters at a news conference. "It is even doubtful if such testimony was actually given."
Court records were not immediately available.
"I will take countermeasures, civil and criminal, against the court witness and the two newspaper companies after an investigation," he said.
It is the second time Mitsuzuka has denied any involvement with the stock speculator. The first time, in 1992, involved allegations by an executive over accepting payments.
The finance minister was appointed as part of Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's new administration following his November victory in the polls.
Soon after his appointment, he acknowledged that a political faction he headed had received political donations from an oil trader currently at the centre of a tax evasion scandal.
Mitsuzuka said the donations were legal and proper and did not constitute a bribe.
